item.title: Envoy and LACI launch EV car-sharing initiative in New Jersey
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The partners will deploy up to 30 shared EVs in Hudson and Bergen counties. An $8.5 million (around €7.8 million) state grant funds the project to expand electric mobility in underserved communities.

item.title: Rolls-Royce Phantom VI swaps V8 for electric powertrain
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Electrogenic has converted a 1973 Rolls-Royce Phantom VI to electric drive. The official representative limousine of the City of London now has 120 kW of power, a 62 kWh battery and charging capacity of up to 100 kW.

item.title: Denza enters India, simultaneously launches D9 and Z9 GT
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: After launching operations in Europe earlier this year, BYD Group's premium and luxury brand Denza has entered the Indian market. The company has launched the D9 MPV and Z9 GT shooting brake as its first two models in the country.

item.title: M&H Carriers deploys 18 new eSprinters for deliveries across northern Scotland
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The Scottish haulier and distributor M&H Carriers has expanded its fleet by 18 new Mercedes-Benz eSprinters. They will be operating across the Highlands and north-east Scotland. With increased range, the new electric vans will be able to manage long routes to remote communities even during cold weather periods.

item.title: Xpeng increases revenue in Q3 2026 to over three billion euros
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Chinese EV manufacturer Xpeng increased its revenue to the equivalent of approximately €3.1 billion in the third quarter of 2026 – a rise of 19.1 per cent compared to the same period last year. In addition to its own vehicle business, the technology partnership with Volkswagen once again contributed to this growth. However, Xpeng continues to post losses.

item.title: Mercedes eActros 600 launches in the Brazilian market
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Mercedes-Benz Trucks is bringing its all-electric eActros 600 truck to the Brazilian market for the first time. Among the first transport companies to deploy the vehicles are fleet customers Bravo Serviços Logísticos, Reiter Log and Ever Express.

item.title: California invests nearly $1.3 billion in clean public transit and rail projects
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: While the bulk of the funding goes towards major rail infrastructure and preserving existing train schedules, targeted grants will deploy more than 75 battery-electric and hydrogen buses, expand microtransit, and support a battery-electric train pilot.

item.title: First manned flight: China’s 19-seat electric aircraft takes off
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The CE-25A electric aircraft from Chinese manufacturer Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (Comac) completed its first manned flight on Saturday. The CE-25A is a joint development by Comac, battery manufacturer CATL, Shanghai Jiao Tong University and other partners.

item.title: Mercedes expands MB.DRIVE with hands-free and lane-change assistants
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Mercedes-Benz will introduce two new motorway assistants in Germany by the end of 2026. Drivers will be allowed to take their hands off the steering wheel at speeds of up to 130 km/h while the car autonomously overtakes or positions itself in the correct lane. Point-to-point driving in the city is expected to become possible from 2027.

item.title: AYK Energy expands business with large marine battery systems
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: AYK Energy is supplying battery systems with a total capacity of 165 MWh for three new all-electric fast ferries operated by Danish shipping company Molslinjen. Each of the catamaran ferries, being built by Incat Tasmania, will receive a 55 MWh system.

item.title: Volkswagen opens pre-orders for ID. Aura L5 in China
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: FAW-Volkswagen has opened pre-orders in China for the new ID. Aura L5. The electric mid-size sedan is based on Volkswagen's CMP platform, offers a range of 580 kilometres according to CLTC, and is expected to launch in 2026.

item.title: WeaveGrid and Hyundai Motor Group partner on US smart charging and V2G
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The US software provider is partnering with Hyundai Motor Group to integrate smart charging and future vehicle-to-grid (V2G) services directly into the myHyundai and Kia Access apps in North America. The joint platform will optimise EV charging times for lower electricity rates while supporting local power grids.

item.title: Toyota recalls C-HR+ worldwide due to battery control unit issue
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Toyota must recall around 19,000 units of its electric C-HR+ worldwide, including 1,096 vehicles in Germany. The reason is a fault in the battery management system which, in the worst case, could cause the electric drivetrain to shut down.

item.title: India: Delhivery to add up to 2,000 electric light commercial vehicles
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Indian logistics service provider Delhivery has announced plans to deploy between 1,500 and 2,000 electric small trucks over the next 12 to 18 months. The company will use the new EVs for its intra-city logistics operations.

item.title: Renault to create 2,000 new jobs in EV production
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: The Renault Group plans to hire 2,000 production workers at its French plants by 2028 to meet growing demand for electric vehicles. At the same time, up to 1,000 jobs in administrative areas are to be cut through voluntary departures.

item.title: Kia launches Carens EV in Indonesia as its first locally built electric model
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: A year after introducing the Carens Clavis EV in India, Kia has launched the model in Indonesia, where it is simply called the Carens EV. The three-row MPV is the company's first locally assembled electric model in the country.

item.title: Tesla announces multi-billion-euro expansion of Gigafactory Grünheide
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Tesla has announced plans to invest three billion euros in expanding its factory in Grünheide, Brandenburg. From 2029, the Tesla Cybercab robotaxi is set to be manufactured there. Battery cell production will also be expanded, with construction work scheduled to begin in 2027.

item.title: Vilnius Airport replaces diesel buses with battery-electric buses
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Vilnius Airport is replacing its entire diesel bus fleet for passenger transfers with twelve electric buses from Cobus. The new vehicles will enter service on 16 November. The investment totals €7.2 million, including maintenance and repairs.

item.title: CATL to become market leader in passenger car battery swapping
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: CATL could become the largest battery swap station operator for passenger cars in China next year. The company plans to have 6,000 stations in operation by 2027. According to Chinese industry portals, this should be enough to overtake Nio’s slower-growing battery swapping network.

item.title: US researchers identify electrode drying risk during fast charging
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Researchers at the University of Maryland have found that lithium ions carry solvent molecules with them as they move through a battery. During fast charging, however, the solvent may not flow back quickly enough, causing the positive electrode to dry out and slowing the charging process.

item.title: ASTAG Charge launches with 100 companies across 60 locations
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The Swiss Commercial Vehicle Association has launched ASTAG Charge, a network that allows members to share their truck charging infrastructure. A total of 100 companies are now participating, providing around 200 charging points for a fleet of 585 electric trucks.

item.title: Lucid cuts cash burn and secures additional $1.75 billion
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Lucid reduced its cash burn by 30 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the previous quarter. At the same time, Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, the Public Investment Fund (PIF), is increasing its financing for the electric carmaker by a further $1.75 billion.

item.title: Kempower plans to cut up to 120 jobs worldwide
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Finnish charging station manufacturer Kempower is planning global job cuts, with up to 120 of its 870 positions potentially affected. The company aims to reduce costs in response to challenging market conditions and restructure its organisation.

item.title: Terawatt Infrastructure opens four fleet charging hubs in the US
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The charging infrastructure provider has added a combined 22 MW of charging capacity across four sites in California, Tennessee, Florida and Texas. According to the company, the new depots can charge more than 3,000 commercial electric vehicles per day.

item.title: Li Auto to enter four new Asian markets and launch right-hand-drive cars
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Chinese carmaker Li Auto is expanding its presence in Asia, with plans to enter Hong Kong, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. The company has also announced its first right-hand-drive models, starting with its flagship Li Mega electric MPV.

item.title: Price jump for Tesla Model Y AWD – base trim no longer available
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: After just over nine months, the entry-level version of the Tesla Model Y AWD has vanished from the configurator. It was the $41,990 option to get a base trim with dual-motor all-wheel drive. Now, the Model Y AWD starts at the Premium trim for $49,990. With rear-wheel drive, the entry-level model still starts at $39,990.

item.title: Visteon, Shinry and Infineon develop single-stage 22 kW onboard charger
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Visteon-Shinry Power Electronics and Infineon are jointly developing a single-stage onboard charger for electric vehicles. The new architecture supports AC charging at up to 22 kW and uses bidirectional GaN switches to achieve a more compact, less complex design than conventional two-stage systems.

item.title: Denmark plans social EV subsidies from 2028
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Denmark is earmarking DKK 3.9 billion (around €521.7 million) for a climate package aimed at making the transition to sustainable transport socially equitable. From 2028, incentives will help low-income households switch to electric cars, including through subsidised leasing. Purchase subsidies are also being considered.

item.title: Tesla Cybercab for private sale comes without steering wheel but with restrictions
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Tesla is inviting “selected customers” to buy Cybercabs for private use at a price of $29,990. However, the car can only be driven with an additional $299-per-month “Autonomy subscription” and is restricted to Tesla's Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida.

item.title: BMW opens battery assembly plant for the new iX5
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: BMW has officially opened its new battery assembly plant in Woodruff, South Carolina, and started series production. The factory assembles the high-voltage batteries for the new BMW iX5, marking an important milestone ahead of the electric SUV's production ramp-up.
